conflicts: Clarity proposes: Create a deliberate left-column sequence by grouping the title, mission brief, and Start Mission action more tightly, with the button directly following the briefing. Visual System & Craft proposes: Rebuild the planet with a deliberate surface vocabulary—clean vector landmasses, controlled atmospheric rim, consistent shadow falloff, and sharper orbital geometry—so it matches the UI's precision. Expressiveness proposes: Give each upgrade a distinct functional icon and micro-visualization, make the mission threat visible through a content-specific enemy trajectory or shield stress cue, and develop the START control as a memorable launch interaction while retaining the disciplined command aesthetic. accept: Accept Clarity's grouping and label-to-object improvements because they make required relationships visibly legible. Accept Craft's cleanup of construction, typography, and state consistency wherever it preserves all required elements. compromise: Start with the fidelity-critical action: Resolve the start-state contradiction by presenting the HUD as an upcoming mission forecast or resetting wave/HP to a pre-launch state. Then adopt the other reviewers' hierarchy, token, and expressive refinements within that preserved requirement map. No requested element may be deleted, cropped, reduced to a label, or visually subordinated below its intended role; simplify presentation and unify styling around the complete artifact instead.
